scope: Batch 2 Phase 1 (Milestones A to C): durable AI Product Builder projects, approved starter registry with provenance, durable source revisions, strict preview readiness and a seven-state preview lifecycle, built on the canonical swarm, pipeline, universal engine and SoftwareAgent path. Disabled by default; nothing is applied, deployed or enabled.

keep: Canonical ExecutionScheduler, tryUniversalBuild and SoftwareAgent/Cline path
Existing ProjectRuntimeManager, live-preview coordinator, signed preview gateway and workspace panel
Existing scaffolds as the first approved starters
Batch 1.5 and Codex migration work untouched
extend: runBuildPipeline accepts a server-supplied builder binding (existing files and commit hook); the universal path never falls through to the legacy generator for a builder project
/api/swarm/execute accepts builderProjectId after server-side ownership verification
Workspace panel gains a Project tab behind NEXT_PUBLIC_XROGA_BUILDER

schemaImpact.rollout: Additive migration (two tables and one function). Not applied by this change; apply through the verified migration workflow after review.
schemaImpact.rollback: DROP FUNCTION public.append_builder_revision and DROP TABLE public.builder_revisions, public.builder_projects. No other table references them.

auth.description: New /api/builder routes require the issued tenant context. builderProjectId on /api/swarm/execute is honoured only after the verified owner matches durable storage; unknown or foreign ids return 404.

tenant.description: New owner-scoped tables with RLS, owner SELECT only for the browser role, and an owner-checked service-only append function. Every store method filters by the verified owner.

approval.description: No external mutation. GitHub, Supabase and Vercel actions are Phase 2 and 3.

credentials.description: Snapshots reject credential files and credential-like content before they become durable. No credential is stored in project rows.

egress.description: No new egress. Readiness probes run inside the existing isolated runtime with the existing preview network policy.

cost.description: Builds run through the existing budget reservation and scheduler. No new paid resource.

billing.description: No payment or subscription path changes.

tests.scope: Spec, starter selection, snapshot safety, idempotent creation, tenant denial, replay and conflict, build outcomes.
Strict readiness against a real HTTP server: 404 route, framework error page, empty body, closed port all fail.
HTTP layer: identity required, body identity ignored, cross-tenant 404.
The migration SQL: uniqueness, gapless numbering, replay, conflict, concurrency, foreign owner, browser grants.

architecture.reason: Adds durable project identity and revisions around the existing canonical path. No scheduler, runtime, preview or agent framework is added.

rollout: Merge only after review. Then apply the migration, enable the canonical engine for builder projects, deploy to the Google runtime and set NEXT_PUBLIC_XROGA_BUILDER=1, each as a separate approved step.
rollback: Disable NEXT_PUBLIC_XROGA_BUILDER. The routes are inert without a builderProjectId. Remove the schema with the rollback statements above.
knownGaps: No live end-to-end run: the canonical engine is off by default and no Google runtime provider is deployed
The SQL is exercised only in the builder-phase1 workflow, not on the development machine
QA, repair, restore, export and GitHub are Phase 2; Supabase and Vercel are Phase 3
placeholderClaimsRemaining: Live preview of a generated application on the Google runtime is unverified

blockers: Migration not applied and canonical engine not enabled
No Google runtime provider deployed (PR #856) for a live preview
Authenticated end-to-end and staged security proof not run for this change
